subject: Contingency & transition playbook for GitHub / JetBrains / Atlassian renewals
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: sales-team@jetbrains.com
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:13:00 -0800
Subject: Planning a contingency + transition playbook for upcoming devtools renewals

Team —

We have three vendor renewals converging in Q1–Q2: GitHub Enterprise, JetBrains, and Atlassian (Jira/Confluence). There are two constraints I want us to plan for: (1) potential SLA/price outcomes that force a partial vendor switch, and (2) a narrow-maintenance window for migrations (we cannot disrupt active on-call/launch cycles).

Requesting a short, executable playbook that covers:
- Minimum acceptable SLA/feature parity per product (who signs off)
- Steps and owners for emergency seat reallocation (30/90/365-day buckets)
- Data export responsibilities and timelines (who owns backups, retention)
- Hot paths for developer access (SSO, license assignment, repo access)

Marissa — can you lead vendor negotiation coordination and confirm which vendors we can reasonably extend for short-term grace periods?
Laura — can you validate the finance pick-up lines (one-time credits, amortization treatment) and confirm procurement deadlines?
Ben — please pull the current license_inventory_2026-11.csv (attached) and flag any single points of failure (critical teams with >30 seats tied to a single contract).

I've looped in JetBrains sales so they can confirm export/transition windows proactively. Once we have a 1-pager we can share with the execs for contingency approval.

Thanks —
Karthik
Head of Dev Platform
Redwood Inference

Attachments: license_inventory_2026-11.csv
From: Emma Ridge <emma.ridge@jetbrains.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: sales-team@jetbrains.com, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 14:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Planning a contingency + transition playbook for upcoming devtools renewals

Hi Karthik / Marissa —

Thanks for the heads up and the inventory file. Quick notes from our side:
- We can provide a 60-day grace/extension on existing licenses if needed while contracts finalize.
- Exports: project settings, keymaps/plugins list, and licensing assignment CSVs can be delivered within 7 business days after request. We cannot export binaries of licensed plugins due to vendor rights, but plugin lists and versions are exportable.
- We have a standard enterprise SLA; if you need a tighter SLA we can propose a one-off SLA addendum (I attached a standard quote PDF).

If you can share a short list of the top 5 teams (by seat count / criticality) we will do a targeted export plan and put a technical lead on standby during the migration window.

Regards,
Emma Ridge
Enterprise Sales Lead — JetBrains

Attachments: JetBrains_quote_Q4_2026.pdf
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Ridge <emma.ridge@jetbrains.com>, Nate Sullivan <nate.sullivan@github.com>, contracts@atlassian.com
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 09 Dec 2026 11:27:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Planning a contingency + transition playbook for upcoming devtools renewals

Thanks Emma —

Looping in GitHub and Atlassian so we can align timelines. High-level ask from our side: we need explicit export/restore runbooks for each product and a commitment on a short-term license extension path (30/60 days) during negotiation. Specific asks:
1) GitHub: repo-level retention/export for org-owned repos (issues, PR history), and temporary token scopes for bulk migrations.
2) Atlassian: Confluence page export and Jira project XML exports. Any known quirks for automation?
3) JetBrains: point noted on plugin binaries — we just need reproducible lists and settings.

Ben — per Karthik's note, see the attached inventory and highlight the three teams that cannot accept downtime for repo access.

We plan to present the contingency 1-pager to Ops and Legal on <Fri 2026-12-17>. Please have redlines and potential mitigation windows by EOD Mon 2026-12-14.

Cheers,
Marissa
Senior Solutions 
Redwood Inference

Attachments: (referenced: JetBrains_quote_Q4_2026.pdf, license_inventory_2026-11.csv)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Emma Ridge <emma.ridge@jetbrains.com>, Nate Sullivan <nate.sullivan@github.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Dec 2026 09:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Planning a contingency + transition playbook for upcoming devtools renewals

Quick scan of the inventory (highlights):
- Core infra & sdk teams: 138 JetBrains seats (PyCharm/IntelliJ) — high criticality, cannot risk >24h authoring outage.
- Platform infra: 62 GitHub seats with heavy history (large monorepos). Migration needs a staged mirror + read-only cutover.
- Support & Docs: 45 Atlassian seats (Confluence) — lower criticality but high content volume for exports.

Proposed short-term actions:
- Immediate: request JetBrains 60-day extension (Emma confirmed 60-day possible).
- Near-term: ask GitHub for a bulk export token & rate guidance; schedule a dry-run for repository mirrors with infra team week of Jan 11.
- Legal/Finance: Laura to confirm whether an extension payment can be capitalized or treated as an operational one-off; we need that by 12/18 to avoid churn to fiscal planning.

I've attached the flagged CSV subset (teams_high_impact.csv) pulled from the inventory.

Ben
Director, GTM Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: teams_high_impact.csv
From: contracts@atlassian.com <contracts@atlassian.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 16:44:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Planning a contingency + transition playbook for upcoming devtools renewals

Hi Marissa / Karthik —

Thanks for the detailed notes. We appreciate the heads-up on potential export needs. We can provide Confluence XML exports and Jira project exports on a per-project basis; typical turnaround for a mid-size tenant is 5–9 business days.

I've attached a draft SLA amendment with our standard redlines highlighted. If you can confirm the top 4 projects you want prioritized we will schedule the exports to align with your Jan dry-run.

Regards,
Atlassian Contracts Team

Attachments: Atlassian_SLA_redlines_20261215.docx
